idea: Simple ways to protect plumbing during renovation
title: Protect Drains During Renovation
description: Simple ways to prevent construction debris from setting inside drain pipes during home remodel work.
image_prompt: Vertical 9:16 photographic view of a bathroom floor under active renovation. In the visual center, a clean 2-inch PVC drain pipe stub-out projects vertically through a concrete subfloor surrounded by unfinished floor tile layout. A bright red mechanical expansion test plug with a metal wing nut is securely inserted and tightened inside the top open end of the PVC pipe to completely seal it shut. Fine dust, dry tile adhesive, and small cement crumbs are scattered on the surrounding rough floor, but the interior of the sealed pipe remains entirely clean and protected. Clean ambient job-site lighting, crisp visual details on the plastic pipe surface and mechanical plug, photorealistic jobsite environment, photorealistic finish, no text, no visual labels, no watermarks, no logos.
visual_story: The visual highlights an open PVC drain stub-out on an active renovation site, securely fitted with a temporary mechanical expansion plug. The viewer notices mortar and drywall dust scattered across the unfinished floor, while the interior of the drain line remains completely clean and isolated. This visually demonstrates how capping exposed pipes prevents heavy, setting construction materials from dropping into the drainage system and causing severe obstructions.

on_image_text.explanation: Unsealed drain stub-outs collect mortar and drywall dust that harden inside traps into solid blockages.
on_image_text.takeaway: Seal all exposed pipe openings before demolition or tiling begins.
